title: Microbiology, B.S. (Eberly College of Science)
notes: General Microbiology option, Cell Biology & Genetics emphasis, University Park. The 'MICRB Elective List A/B/C' pools (17 credits total) are modeled as generic slots, same convention as BIOL's 400-level elective groups. 'etm' marks the gateway courses (Chem I, Calc I, MICRB 201) everything downstream depends on. Post-parens-fix re-scrape revealed CHEM 110's real prereq is MATH 22 (a placement threshold below Calc I that a MATH-140-track student has already tested past, but the bulletin's prereq text never says so explicitly), and MATH 22 has its own real chain (MATH 22 needs MATH 21, which needs MATH 4, which needs MATH 3). Added MATH 3 (Semester 1), MATH 4 (Semester 2), MATH 21 (Semester 3), and MATH 22 (Semester 4) explicitly to complete the real chain, matching the fix used for MATSCI/ME/METEO's identical CHEM 110 gap -- this is necessary and correct regardless of the issue below. UNRESOLVED (flagged for human review, not force-fixed): even with this real chain added, the plan cannot reach graduation in 4 years, and no fix within this file can change that. MICRB 201 (the department's own required intro course, no alternative) requires CHEM 110 directly, so it can't be scheduled before Semester 6 in the best case. From there BMB 402 (Semester 6 item) sits behind its own genuinely deep, unavoidable real chain: BMB 402 needs BMB 401, which needs CHEM 210 AND CHEM 212 (CHEM 212 needs CHEM 210, which needs CHEM 112, which needs CHEM 110) AND BMB 251-or-equivalent (every listed equivalent -- BIOL 230M/W, BME 201, MICRB 251 -- itself ultimately needs CHEM 110/112 too, so there is no shorter real alternate route, unlike ME 340's BME 409 escape). Verified structurally (not a credit-cap issue -- confirmed by test-running this plan with max_credits_per_semester temporarily set arbitrarily high, which still produced exactly 10 terms): the minimum real critical path from MATH 3 to BMB 402 is MATH 3 -> MATH 4 -> MATH 21 -> MATH 22 -> CHEM 110 -> MICRB 201 -> BMB 251 -> CHEM 210 -> CHEM 212 -> BMB 401 -> BMB 402, exactly 10 sequential single-prereq terms, 2 more than the 8-term/4-year goal allows. This means test_full_plan_reaches_graduation_in_four_years (tests.py, TestMicrobiologyPlan) cannot pass against the now-correct catalog data without either inventing a fake prereq/course (not done here) or the test's own 4-year assumption being revisited -- left for human review rather than guessed at. 2026-08-27 verification against the live bulletin confirmed the common-requirement credit math: 'Select 3 credits from MICRB Elective List A (Applied)' + 'Select 3 credits from MICRB Elective List B' + 'Select 11 credits from MICRB Elective List C (free electives)' (common, all options) plus the General Microbiology option's own additional 'Select 6 credits from MICRB Elective List B' = List A 3cr / List B 9cr / List C 11cr, 23cr total. This plan's List A (1 slot, 3cr) and List B (3 slots, 9cr) already matched exactly; List C (4 slots) totaled 12cr against the real 11cr, so one slot was reduced from 3 to 2cr (see that item's own notes). The exact course-by-course membership of Lists A/B/C isn't published anywhere in the public bulletin text (it's referenced but not enumerated, and the department's own internal handbook/checksheet with the full lists wasn't found on a public page), so these remain generic unfillable slots rather than match/open_elective picks -- wiring them to open_elective without knowing the real list would risk recommending courses far outside microbiology (as happened and was caught/fixed during this same session's PHYS verification), which is worse than leaving them as an honest placeholder.
